key: And he shall dwell in that city, until he stand before the congregation for judgment, until the death of the high priest that shall be in those days; then may the manslayer return, and come unto his own city, and unto his own house, unto the city from whence he fled.’
s: The LORD bids Joshua set apart cities where one who kills unawares may flee the avenger; Radak, on 20:6, explains with the sages why the slayer stays until the high priest dies, since one who shortens life should not stand before him who lengthens it.

reason: verse.js ok, ref Joshua 20:6 and at [206,6] match. Plain sense faithful: chapter 20 opens with the LORD telling Joshua to have Israel assign cities of refuge for one who kills unawares, a refuge from the avenger of blood (20:1 to 5); no four-word run from the key verse. Read the whole chapter 20 packet (Rashi, Radak, Metzudat David; no Midrash Rabbah on Joshua). Radak on 20:6 explains the court procedure and then gives the reason for ‘until the death of the high priest’ as the sages explained it, quoting Rabbi Meir: the slayer shortens life, the high priest lengthens it, and the shortener should not be before the lengthener (he adds a second reason in Rabbi’s name, which the sentence leaves aside without misrepresenting). ‘explains with the sages’ keeps the attribution honest: Radak reports the rabbinic reason.
